definitions.description: Typed event emitted by Anthropic Batch Finished.
definitions.documentation: Event output contract for Anthropic Batch Finished. Read-only GET https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages/batches/{batchId}, using a named encrypted API key, pinned anthropic-version 2023-06-01 and optional authorized workspace ID. Each invocation makes exactly one bounded request, never creates/cancels a batch or fetches model output. First observation seeds a baseline by default; emitExisting=true emits an already-ended batch once. Running/canceling statuses skip. An observed transition to ended emits counts. Scope changes reset baseline; a single bounded checkpoint commits on success before downstream completion. Errors/429 fail without automatic retry; workflow polling interval controls the next explicit invocation. Response 64 KiB, 1024 chunks and 100–30000ms total deadline. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing

ingressRequirements.description: Outbound read-only polling of one explicitly configured existing Message Batch; no batch creation or model execution.
setupSteps: Install this reviewed package release; installation does not call the provider or start polling.
Save required provider credentials in Infrastructure → Secrets and configure the node with secret names only.
Configure the existing batchId, API-key secret name and optional workspaceId. Authorize that key only for the intended workspace.
Use an interval appropriate to batch duration and API limits (60 seconds is a practical initial choice). Default emitExisting=false seeds the first status without emitting historical completion.
This watches exactly one batch and retains a single scope/status checkpoint. It does not list batches, retrieve results, create/cancel work, acknowledge a queue or run a model.
Create an outbound polling ingress profile, review its network/setup plan and bind this trigger node.
Set the saved entry kind to poll and an appropriate interval of at least five seconds; enable workflow and entry deliberately.
Review first-run, cursor and bounded deduplication semantics. Checkpoints commit on trigger success before downstream completion; downstream failure does not restore them.
